title: Sooke Region Museum

services.name: School Tours
services.desc: The Sooke Region Museum provides educational school programs for students from Kindergarten to Grade 8. We have specialized tour experiences tailored for specific grades to complement the BC Curricular Competencies. Activity descriptions are below on this page and in the downloadable pdf. We can accommodate 2 classes per visit. Kindergarten to Grade 5 classes participate in four 15-minute activities + a 30-minute activity where they cook bannock in the fireplace and have time for snacks they bring. Teachers book the other 4 activities on the booking form. Grades 6-7-8 participate in four 30-minute activities. One of these activities is a block where they will cook bannock in the fireplace

services.name: Summer Camps
services.desc: 3. Just want to try the activities and not stay for the full morning? Activities are set up at the Museum from 9am-12pm, priced individually, all ages (yes, that means adults too!) Kids will participate in fun skill-building workshops. Outdoor time and games included - all on the grounds and in the historic buildings of the Sooke Region Museum. Skill-building sessions will focus on homesteading skills inspired by Moss Cottage, including making butter, bread, jam, sewing - life skills just as important today as they were in 1902! Choose your own activities - 9am-12pm, any days between 10 and 21 August - $45 per

services.name: Past Exhibits
services.desc: Uncover the mystery of the Lord Western shipwreck! Or learn about west coast lighthouses with the Triangle Island Lighthouse. In the latter half the 20th century, the Sooke region was at the heart of some of the major forestry projects on Vancouver Island. Learn about the Sooke region’s magnificent forests and what makes them so special. Did you know the Sooke region is home to Greater Victoria’s water supply? The Flowline was a master feat of engineering for it’s time in 1911-1915 and was built with no electricity! On the museum grounds are heritage buildings and equipment. These historic pieces helped shape and build the Sooke to what it is today. Take a trip back in time in Moss Cottage,
